title: The Claude 3 Model Family
hook: Anthropic's Claude 3 family offers a three-tier speed-capability tradeoff - Haiku, Sonnet, Opus - with multimodal input and alignment built on Constitutional AI methods.
key_points: Three models (Haiku, Sonnet, Opus) trade off inference speed against raw capability, letting users pick the right point on the cost curve.
All three accept image inputs alongside text, making the full family multimodal.
Opus set a new benchmark high for Anthropic at release, exceeding GPT-4 on several academic evals.
Alignment approach draws on Constitutional AI: models are trained with a set of principles rather than purely on human preference labels.
content_html: Anthropic released the Claude 3 model family in March 2024, comprising three models — Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus — designed to cover different points on the speed-versus-capability spectrum. All three accept image and text inputs. Opus, the largest and most capable, outperformed competing frontier models on a range of academic benchmarks at launch.
extra_html:
How it works

The Claude 3 models are large transformer-based language models trained with Anthropic's Constitutional AI approach: rather than relying solely on human preference comparisons, the models are guided during training by a written set of principles, helping the model reason about what a helpful and harmless response looks like. Multimodal input is handled through a vision encoder that processes images alongside the text context.

Why it matters

The tiered family design makes it practical to choose the right model for a task — cheap and fast for high-volume or latency-sensitive work, more capable for complex reasoning — without switching providers. Constitutional AI as the alignment backbone also represents a different philosophy to RLHF-only approaches. See Anthropic's announcement for benchmark details and availability.
